\chapter{Chapter08 — Product Lp Inequalities}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter08.ProductLpInequalities
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter08.ProductLpInequalities}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Positive sign mass]
\lean{FABL.pmfSignPlusMass}
\label{FABL.pmfSignPlusMass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $Ω$ be a finite set, let $π$ be a probability mass function on $Ω$, and let
$f:Ω\to\mathbb R$. The positive sign mass of $f$ under $π$ is the probability that
$f(x)=1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Negative sign mass]
\lean{FABL.pmfSignMinusMass}
\label{FABL.pmfSignMinusMass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $Ω$ be a finite set, let $π$ be a probability mass function on $Ω$, and let
$f:Ω\to\mathbb R$. The negative sign mass of $f$ under $π$ is the probability that
$f(x)=-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative mass at plus one]
\lean{FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_nonneg}
\label{FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation_nonneg, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. The probability mass assigned to points where $f(x)=1$ is
nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative mass at minus one]
\lean{FABL.pmfSignMinusMass_nonneg}
\label{FABL.pmfSignMinusMass_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation_nonneg, FABL.pmfSignMinusMass}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. The probability mass assigned to points where $f(x)=-1$ is
nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Masses at the two signs sum to one]
\lean{FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_add_minus}
\label{FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_add_minus}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfSignMinusMass, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. The probability masses of
the points where $f$ equals $1$ and where $f$ equals $-1$ sum to $1$.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. The expectation of $f$
equals the probability that $f=1$ minus the probability that $f=-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute moments of sign deviations]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_eq_signPlusMass_sub_minus, FABL.pmfExpectation_mul_const, FABL.pmfSignMinusMass, FABL.pmfSignMinusMass_nonneg, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_add_minus, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_nonneg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$. For any real $p$, write $a=\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\pi}(f(x)=1)$ and
$b=\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\pi}(f(x)=-1)$. Then
\[\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}\bigl[|f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}f(y)|^p\bigr]=a(2b)^p+b(2a)^p.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance of a sign-valued random variable]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_sq_sub_mean}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_sq_sub_mean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow, FABL.pmfSignMinusMass, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_add_minus}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. Then the expectation of
the squared deviation of $f$ from its mean is four times the product of the
probabilities that $f$ equals $1$ and $-1$:
$\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[(f-\mathbb{E}_{\pi}f)^2]=4\,\mathbb{P}_{\pi}(f=1)\,\mathbb{P}_{\pi}(f=-1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power bound for two nonnegative parts]
\lean{FABL.two_rpow_sub_one_mul_add_rpow_le_one}
\label{FABL.two_rpow_sub_one_mul_add_rpow_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $a,b,r\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $a,b\ge 0$, $a+b=1$, and $0\le r\le 1$. Then
$2^{r-1}(a^r+b^r)\le 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moment bound for sign deviations]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow_le_sq}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow_le_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasSignRange, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow, FABL.pmfExpectation_sq_sub_mean, FABL.pmfSignMinusMass, FABL.pmfSignMinusMass_nonneg, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_add_minus, FABL.pmfSignPlusMass_nonneg, FABL.two_rpow_sub_one_mul_add_rpow_le_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$. For every real $p$ with $1\le p\le2$, the $p$th absolute
moment of the deviation from the mean is at most the variance:
\[\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}\bigl[|f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}f(y)|^p\bigr]\le\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}\bigl[(f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}f(y))^2\bigr].\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power bound for a bounded real number]
\lean{FABL.abs_rpow_le_two_rpow_mul_sq}
\label{FABL.abs_rpow_le_two_rpow_mul_sq}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For real numbers $z$ and $p$, if $|z|\le2$ and $p\ge2$, then $|z|^p\le 2^p z^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moment bound for sign-valued functions]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow_le_two_rpow_mul_sq}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_sub_mean_rpow_le_two_rpow_mul_sq}

\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. For every real $p\ge 1$,
the expectation of $|f-\mathbb E_\pi f|^p$ is at most $2^p$ times the expectation of
$(f-\mathbb E_\pi f)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate conditional absolute moment]
\lean{FABL.coordinateConditionalAbsMoment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b002}
\label{FABL.coordinateConditionalAbsMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability distribution $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\Omega^n$. For a real number $p$,
coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and input $x\in\Omega^n$, define the coordinate
conditional absolute moment as the expectation over $\omega\sim\pi$ of
$|f(x_{-i},\omega)-m|^p$, where $m$ is the expectation of $f(x_{-i},\omega)$ and
$x_{-i}$ denotes $x$ with coordinate $i$ replaced by $\omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional absolute moment as a coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.coordinateConditionalAbsMoment_eq_coordinateProjection}
\label{FABL.coordinateConditionalAbsMoment_eq_coordinateProjection}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateConditionalAbsMoment, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.coordinateProjection_apply, FABL.coordinateProjection_replaceCoordinate, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productCoordinateLaplacian, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, let $n\ge 0$, let
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and choose $p\in\mathbb R$, a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
and $x\in\Omega^n$. The $p$th absolute moment of $f$ about its mean when only coordinate
$i$ is resampled according to $\pi$ equals the average, over that coordinate, of
$|f-\mathbb E_i f|^p$, where $\mathbb E_i f$ denotes the same coordinate average of $f$
with all other coordinates fixed at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Laplacian moment as a conditional moment]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_abs_laplacian_rpow_eq_conditional}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_abs_laplacian_rpow_eq_conditional}

\difficulty{3}
Let $[?]$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $[?]$, and let a
finite nonempty index set label an orthonormal basis of real functions on that set
containing the constant-one function. For a positive integer $n$, a real exponent $p$, a
function $f$ on $[?]^n$, and a coordinate $i$, define the conditional centered $p$th
absolute moment at $x$ by averaging
$|f(x_{-i},\omega)-\mathbb{E}_{\omega'}f(x_{-i},\omega')|^p$ over $[?]$, where $x_{-i}$
denotes all coordinates other than $i$. Then the product-measure mean of $|L_i f|^p$,
where $L_i f$ is $f$ minus its average over coordinate $i$, equals the product-measure
mean of this conditional centered moment.
\end{theorem}

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the product $L^p$ norm]
\lean{FABL.productLpNorm_nonneg}
\label{FABL.productLpNorm_nonneg}

\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation_nonneg, FABL.pmfLpNorm, FABL.productLpNorm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$n$ be a natural number, let $p\in\mathbb R$, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The
product $L^p$ quantity
\[
\left(\mathbb E\,|f|^p\right)^{1/p}
\]
is nonnegative, where the expectation is taken under the independent product
distribution with marginal $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power of the product-space norm]

The $p$th power of the product-space $L^p$ norm of $f$ equals the product-distribution

\end{theorem}

$p\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le p$, and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Writing $\mathbb E_\pi
f=\sum_{x\in\Omega}\pi(x)f(x)$, one has $|\mathbb E_\pi f|^p\le \mathbb E_\pi(|f|^p)$.

\begin{definition}[Anisotropic product noise kernel]
\lean{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseKernel}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p064-b001
}
\label{FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseKernel}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.productCoordinateNoisePMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability distribution $\pi$, and let $n$ be a
natural number. Given an input $x\in\Omega^n$ and coordinate parameters $\rho_i\in[0,1]$
for every $i$, define the anisotropic product noise kernel to be the probability
distribution on $\Omega^n$ obtained by independently applying the coordinate noise
distribution with parameter $\rho_i$ to $x_i$ at each coordinate $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Anisotropic noise on a product basis function]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.pmfExpectation_anisotropicProductNoiseKernel_productFunction}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.pmfExpectation_anisotropicProductNoiseKernel_productFunction}

\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$, with
distinguished constant basis index $0_B$. Choose coordinate parameters $\rho_i\in[0,1]$
for $i=1,\ldots,n$, a point $x\in\Omega^n$, and a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$. The
expectation of the product basis function indexed by $a$ under the coordinatewise noise
distribution at $x$ is $\left(\prod_{i=1}^n c_i\right)\prod_{i=1}^n B_{a_i}(x_i)$, where
$c_i=1$ if $a_i=0_B$ and $c_i=\rho_i$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean preservation by anisotropic noise]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zeroMultiIndex, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator, FABL.productMean}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the
constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, any function
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and any choice of real coordinate parameters
$\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_n$, the product mean of the anisotropic product noise operator
applied to $f$ equals the product mean of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Anisotropic noise hypercontractivity]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.abs_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator_rpow_le}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.abs_anisotropicProductNoiseOperator_rpow_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator_apply_eq_pmfExpectation, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.abs_pmfExpectation_rpow_le, FABL.anisotropicProductNoiseOperator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with one basis vector equal to the constant function
$1$. For $n\ge 0$, let $T_\rho$ act on functions on $\Omega^n$ by multiplying each
product Fourier coefficient at index $a\in\iota^n$ by $\prod_{i:a_i\ne 0}\rho_i$, where
$0$ denotes the constant basis index. If $0\le \rho_i\le 1$ for every coordinate, $p\ge
1$, and $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, then $|T_\rho f(x)|^p\le T_\rho(|f|^p)(x)$ for every
$x\in\Omega^n$.
